jobs.title: Information Security Analyst
jobs.description:
Primary Duties And Responsibilities

General Electric Credit Union is a not-for-profit, member-owned full service financial institution headquartered in Cincinnati with branches in Ohio and Kentucky. At GECU, we pride ourselves on maintaining quality service, being an employee-friendly workplace, and developing our team members while teaching you the skills to lead you to career advancement opportunities.

Overview

The Information Security Analyst supplements the role of the Information Security Manager. This role plays an integral part in supporting the implementation and maintenance of the credit union’s information security program by providing administrative support, monitoring security systems, and conducting vulnerability assessments to protect the security of GECU’s information systems as well as the confidentiality of information assets.

Essential Responsibilities

Administer and maintain key information security systems, such as incident response, phishing and security training, log monitoring and vulnerability scanning platforms
Respond to reports of phishing messages and notify team members of malicious messages
Assist the Information Security Manager with the generation of reports and documentation for regulatory bodies
Assist the Information Security Manager with the completion of audits, risk assessments, and incident response actions
Assist with the formation of information security strategies for the protection of sensitive data
Stay updated on the latest security threats and trends within the industry to respond to emerging cyber threats
Collaborate with the IT Department to ensure that new projects or implementations of new technologies are secure in nature
Support compliance with applicable laws and regulations, including but not limited to the Bank Secrecy Act, Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA), and NCUA Rule 12 CFR Part 748.
Performs other duties to support the department as necessary

Education And Experience

High school diploma or GED required; Associate or bachelor’s degree in information technology or Cybersecurity preferred
1-3 years of experience in information security or related field
Certifications such as CompTIA Security+ or equivalent are preferred

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong verbal and written communications skills with the ability to work in a team environment
Thorough knowledge and understanding of Information Security policies and procedures
Good organizational skills
Basic knowledge of information security principles, practices, and technologies
Familiarity with regulatory compliance requirements and industry standards
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities
Familiarity with navigating web-based applications and making administrative changes using a Graphical User Interface (GUI)
Proficiency in security tools and technologies, such as firewalls and intrusion detection systems
Basic computer troubleshooting and hardware
Familiarity with computing systems in a regulated corporate environment
Understanding of basic computing and network principles (IP Addresses, Hostnames, Operating System versions, etc.)

At GECU, we want to support your wellbeing by offering a wide range of benefits:

Health, Dental and Vision insurance
Life and Disability insurance options
Paid Time Off starts accruing once hired and take your birthday off -paid
401k Retirement plan with up to a 10% match of your base gross compensation
Tuition reimbursement opportunities & professional development
Volunteer opportunities -and earn additional PTO hours!
On-site clinics for Vaccines and Mammograms

And many more!

Come join GECU as we are a curated culture of respect, understanding, and mutual recognition. We believe forming bonds and connecting with each other only stands to strengthen the service we provide to our members in our mission of improving the Quality of Financial lives!

General Electric Credit Union is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.

What We Offer

Salary:

$108,000.00 - $148,500.00

Location:

Austin,TX

You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.

Applied Materials is seeking an experienced Compliance Project Manager. The role will be at the Austin office and is onsite (not remote or hybrid).

Role Overview

As a key member of the Strategy Office, you will own how the Global Supply Chain responds to product and environmental regulatory requirements — surveying the supply base, interpreting what the results mean for Applied's products, and driving the sourcing and engineering actions that follow. This role suits a supply chain professional who can read a complex data set and determine what to do about it: someone who turns supplier survey results into prioritized supplier, sourcing and engineering actions, and carries those actions to closure across a matrixed global organization.

Must have supply chain, procurement or sourcing experience.
Must have strong data analysis and reporting skills.
Must have experience influencing and presenting data to executive level.

Key Responsibilities

Supply Base Survey & Data Management: Own the supply base survey process — determine which suppliers, parts and materials to survey and to what level of detail, drive collection across the supply base, and hold suppliers accountable for complete, accurate and timely responses.
Analytics & Reporting: Analyze large and complex supplier and product data sets using advanced analytics tools (Excel, Databricks, Tableau etc.) to identify exposure, risk and gaps. Develop the reporting that drives compliance and cost initiatives and informs sourcing decisions.
Action Translation & Execution: Convert survey findings into prioritized supplier, sourcing and engineering actions — coordinating part changes, supplier requirements and engineering change with Supplier Account Management, Supplier Engineering, the Design Engineering Authority and the Business Unit materials through implementation.
Regulatory Compliance: Serve as the Global Supply Chain point of contact for product and environmental regulatory requirements, including US-EPA/TSCA and EU/REACH, partnering with the Compliance Legal team on formal interpretation and with EHS as needed.
Project Management: Lead and manage multiple compliance projects and programs simultaneously, applying best-in-class methodologies to ensure successful delivery of outcomes, milestones and resource allocation.
Communication & Influence: Communicate complex findings and recommendations clearly and persuasively to stakeholders at all levels. Create impactful presentations and facilitate meetings to drive consensus and decision-making.
Continuous Improvement & Documentation: Identify and implement process improvements that reduce manual effort and improve data quality. Ensure all phases of project, program and process development are documented and disseminated to the relevant functional areas.

Required Skills & Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree preferred.
7–10 years of experience in material management, procurement, sourcing, program management or analytics within a matrixed or global organization.
Demonstrated ability to interpret supplier and product data and translate findings into actionable supplier, sourcing and engineering outcomes.
Advanced proficiency in Excel (formulas, pivot tables, data visualization) and PowerPoint (presentation design and storytelling); experience with Databricks, Tableau, Power BI or SQL preferred.
Professional certifications (e.g., PMP, CAPM, Six Sigma) are a plus.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to influence and build relationships across diverse teams and geographies.
Strong problem-solving, critical-thinking and stakeholder management abilities.
Familiarity with product or environmental regulatory requirements is an advantage but not required; the right supply chain professional will be developed on the regulatory detail.

Impact Statement

This role is pivotal in keeping Applied's products compliant and its supply base able to supply them. Your analysis, and the actions you drive from it, will directly influence sourcing decisions, product change and the company's regulatory standing.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Critical Harm Operations
jobs.description:
About The Team

Critical Harm Operations sits within User Safety & Risk Operations and builds enforcement systems for Frontier Risk and Material Harm that are accurate, fast, defensible, and built to scale. We turn policy intent into operational readiness, review standards, quality systems, escalation paths, automation guardrails, and durable cross-functional operating models.

About The Role

We are looking for an exceptional Program Manager to help build durable operating systems and run some of OpenAI’s most complex safety operations. The core need is a high-agency operator who can take an ambiguous problem, create the right structure, align cross-functional partners, and drive the work through execution.

This role will move across Critical Harm priorities as needs evolve. You may step into operationalizing national security or violent-activities workflows, support wellbeing and Frontier Risk initiatives, or help scale programs such as Trusted Access. Deep domain expertise is helpful but not required; the strongest candidates will learn quickly, exercise excellent judgment, and make complex programs move.

In This Role, You Will

Lead strategic operational builds across priority workflows from problem statement to implemented operating model, including scope, owners, milestones, risks, success measures, and execution cadence.
Translate policy, safety, technical, legal, and operational constraints into workflows, requirements, playbooks, escalation paths, and decision-making structures that teams can execute.
Coordinate with User Ops leadership, Product Policy, Integrity, Safety Systems, i2, Legal, Product, Engineering, Support, vendors, and other partners to resolve dependencies and keep critical work moving.
Move in and out of workflows as priorities shift—standing up new programs, stabilizing operations, improving handoffs, and transitioning durable ownership to the right team.
Use operational data and frontline signals to identify bottlenecks, quality gaps, capacity needs, ownership failures, and the highest-leverage interventions.
Drive high-priority escalations and cross-functional decisions to closure, ensuring the right context, accountable owners, clear next steps, and durable follow-up.
Create the mechanisms that make programs run well: roadmaps, decision logs, status updates, risk registers, operating reviews, and crisp executive communication.
Identify where AI tools, automation, lightweight systems, or simpler workflows can improve speed, consistency, and scale while preserving appropriate human judgment.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have deep expertise with national security, violence, Threat-to-life or other severe-harm domains.
Have 8+ years of experience in program management, strategy and operations, product operations, technical program management, trust and safety, support operations, risk operations, implementation, or a related field.
Have a track record of taking complex, ambiguous work from problem framing through launch and scaled operation.
Are unusually organized, sharp, and execution-focused; you can manage many moving pieces without losing the few decisions that matter most.
Build trust and drive alignment across teams without direct authority, while keeping ownership, accountability, and escalation paths clear.
Are technically and analytically fluent enough to reason about data flows, dashboards, tooling gaps, automation, and failure modes—even if you are not writing production code.
Communicate clearly with technical, operational, policy, and executive audiences, especially when tradeoffs are sensitive or evidence is incomplete.
Operate calmly and flexibly in a fast-moving environment, learn new domains quickly, and are comfortable handling high-severity or sensitive work.
Experience with vendor operations, QA programs, launch readiness, workflow automation, or AI-assisted operations.

Nice To Have

Experience in customer support or other high-stakes scaled operations.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Requirements

Project Manager

At Fearless, we are seeking a Project Manager to lead delivery of a new AI-enabled document review and governance platform for a federal agency. The platform supports critical funding oversight and must reach production readiness within 90 days through three tightly integrated 30-day increments. As the single point of contact for the Government contracting team, you will own the integrated schedule, manage dependencies that span Government-furnished systems and AI platform access, and run the team's Agile cadence as Scrum Master to keep delivery on track. This is a remote role. Candidates must live within commuting distance of Washington, DC and be available to attend on-site meetings as directed by the customer.

As a Project Manager, you manage and integrate multiple projects to deliver a single, impactful outcome. You operate independently, providing world-class service that drives account growth and ensures positive net customer retention across all assigned project offices. This role involves overseeing project delivery and leading and mentoring team members, equipping them with the skills necessary to be effective in their roles. You will foster collaboration and excellence, ensuring successful project outcomes while contributing to the organization's strategic growth.

Fearless Your Responsibilities In This Role:

Own the integrated schedule across three 30-day increments, managing day-30, day-60, and day-90 delivery gates to ensure the minimum viable product reaches production on time.
Maintain a dependency register tracking equipment, accounts, environments, identity test access, AI platform access, prototype handover, and reference data, with dates requested at kickoff.
Serve as the main point of contact for the Contracting Officer and COR, coordinating with designated Government stakeholders to resolve blockers and align expectations.
Deliver against the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP), produce monthly status reports, and maintain the risk and opportunity register to protect schedule commitments.
Run sprint and increment ceremonies as Scrum Master and Agile delivery lead, ensuring the team maintains velocity and surfaces impediments early.
Manage staffing, onboarding, security processing, and any key personnel substitution requests to keep the team fully operational throughout the contract.
Plan requirements workshops with the Product Designer and track follow-ups with Government stakeholders to ensure shared understanding and timely decisions.
Coordinate production go-live, training, and handover with the team to ensure a smooth transition to operations and sustained platform success.

Customer & Fearless Impact:

The Impact You Will Create in this Role:

A Successful Candidate In This Role Can Independently Operate With Little To No Support From Their Leadership In Day-to-day Tasks And Decision-making. This Team Member Will Also Proactively Understand The Implications Of Their Decision-making And Be Able To Convey It Through Their Project Strategy And Day-to-day Influence. This Project Manager Will Impact Fearless’ Customers By:

Effectively managing and integrating multiple projects, you will deliver impactful outcomes that drive customer satisfaction and account growth. Y
Enhancing team performance, ensuring that each project is executed to the highest standard.
Contributing to positive net customer retention, reinforcing the organization’s reputation for excellence in the account industry, project assigned.
Ensure that Fearless positively impacts our customers' missions and the lives of the people they serve by consistently delivering world-class products and services on time and within budget.

Work Experience

PROJECT SKILL AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

Required Experience

Minimum of 8 years managing software delivery, including at least 3 years on federal IT contracts.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.
U.S. citizen, willing and able to obtain and maintain a Top Secret clearance (Tier 5 investigation). The clearance process will begin at contract start.
PMP or PMI-ACP certification, plus a Scrum certification (CSM or PSM) is required.
Proven track record running at least one fixed-price or fixed-schedule Agile delivery from contract award through to accepted release.
Demonstrated ability managing Government-furnished dependencies such as environments, accounts, and security reviews, and shepherding an ATO or security package through to an authorizing official's decision.
Hands-on background serving as Scrum Master or running Agile ceremonies for cross-functional software delivery teams.
Experience serving as the primary point of contact for a Contracting Officer and COR, including formal reporting and deliverable acceptance.
Experience producing status reports, integrated schedules, and risk and issue registers for Government stakeholders.
Experience onboarding staff onto federal contracts, including coordinating clearance or background investigation processing.

Preferred Experience

Federal budget oversight or grants-management programs involving funding announcements, 2 CFR 200, or Grants.gov.
Delivery inside an on-premises or closed-network Government environment.
Background delivering AI/ML or LLM-enabled products with human-in-the-loop review workflows.
Familiarity with performance-based contracting structures, including QASPs and milestone-based acceptance criteria.
Current or active Top Secret clearance (T5), in access within the last 24 months

Fearless Skills And Competencies

Communicating with Credibility & Influence: Builds credibility as a subject matter expert within the customer’s organization. Promotes buy-in among organizational stakeholders for initiatives. Motivates staff and other stakeholders to support vision and goals. Serves as an advocate for the organization or team members to advance the organization’s strategic direction and goals. Shares opinions about important issues, regardless of risk or discouragement from others. Promotes the role of their function in achieving the organization’s mission, vision, and goals. Builds credibility for themselves and is Fearless within the customer’s organization as an expert in their field. Serves as an influential voice for strategies, philosophies, and initiatives within the organization. Advocates for the implementation of evidence-based solutions. Inspires staff, customers, and executive-level organizational stakeholders to support and pursue the organization’s strategic direction, vision and long-term goals. Builds consensus among leaders about the organization’s strategic direction and long-term goals. Uses knowledge and skills to influence business strategy.
Technology Awareness: Wholistic knowledge of technology developments and new applications (hardware, software, telecommunications), emerging technologies and ability to apply to business processes and implementation of information systems to meet organizational requirements.
Project Management for Gov Contracts: Applies project management principles and practices to plan, execute, and close government projects, ensuring timely delivery, budget adherence, and compliance with federal regulations.
Account Growth & Retention: Nurtures, grows and maintains existing accounts by monitoring, measuring, and ensuring customer satisfaction; leveraging existing contracts for up-selling and cross-selling opportunities, actively troubleshooting and resolving issues, countering competitive threats, and expanding customer networks and champions.
Government Procurement Rules, Regulations & Methods: Uses knowledge of contracting officers, acquisition regulations, procurement levels, and government contracting methods—including contract types, IDIQ, GSA schedules, socio-economic categories, and teaming agreements—to identify opportunities and secure funding that align with the organization’s strategic priorities, ensuring successful outcomes for both the organization and its customers.
Evaluating Business Challenges: Partners with stakeholders to understand current and future challenges, and identify needs and opportunities for improvement. Informs stakeholders about current and future threats and liabilities that jeopardize successful outcomes. Advises stakeholders through collaboration and recommends solutions to ensure attainment of business outcomes and support the organization’s strategic direction and long-term goals.

Integrates solutions with related organizational processes, systems, and other business or management initiatives.

Conducts performance reviews and career planning, removes demotivating factors in the environment, and enhances collective team competencies.

Cost Estimation & Budgeting: Develops accurate cost estimates and budgets for government projects, ensuring compliance with federal financial management regulations and guidelines.
Environmental & Customer Awareness: Maintains awareness of agency and other external dynamics, power structures within client environments as well as functional/domain knowledge, regulatory trends and contract requirements that influence service delivery and company expansion/growth.

Umbra is an American space technology company delivering advanced systems, from sensors to spacecraft, that empower customers worldwide with unmatched access to critical information from space. Our mission is simple and ambitious: redefine space—for people, systems, and missions in every domain. Umbra's ecosystem operates through three business units: Remote Sensing (the data), Space Systems (the components), and Mission Solutions (the platforms). Together, our teams develop capabilities that deliver persistent access, resilient performance, and mission-ready solutions, advancing U.S. space leadership while keeping the world safe and informed.

About The Team

Mission Solutions - The Platforms

Mission Solutions builds on Umbra's expertise in remote sensing and spacecraft operations to engineer platforms purpose-built for U.S. and allied defense and intelligence missions. Whether it's a custom payload, a full-stack spacecraft, or the infrastructure behind an entire constellation, our team delivers secure, resilient systems tailored to exacting requirements and built on timelines that match the urgency of the mission.

If you want to work on cutting-edge space technology that's redefining what's possible in space platforms, you belong here at Umbra.

About The Job

As a Program Manager
, you will be responsible for delivering exceptional products, systems, services, and solutions that exceed customer expectations across cost, schedule, and technical performance. The position requires a strong understanding of how technical, financial, and organizational elements align to drive program success, including the development of structured roadmaps, schedules, and budgets that are actively managed throughout the program lifecycle.

The Program Manager will work closely with Umbra's product management team to define development scope and ensure execution aligns with the principles of the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe). Success in this role depends on effective communication across both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including providing concise leadership updates and maintaining strong customer relationships. A deep understanding of Umbra's technologies enables informed oversight of technical progress and proactive management of risks and challenges.

In addition to program execution, you will contribute to business development activities, including proposals, RFI responses, customer engagement, and organic growth initiatives. The Program Manager also serves as a capture manager, leading capture strategy and proposal development for pursuits of varying size and complexity that align with Umbra's strategic campaigns.

This position is based on-site in either our Arlington, VA office or Reston, VA office.

Key Responsibilities

Program Execution: Take complete responsibility for the successful implementation (including cost, schedule, and technical aspects) of several ongoing contracts. Ensure monthly updates of financial results and forecasts. Deliver monthly status reports to facilitate Program Management Reviews.
Processes: Participate in the maturation of Umbra's Program Excellence Framework, which consists of documented procedures for initiating, executing, and concluding programs. Utilize insights and experiences gained from previous programs, while customizing them to align with Umbra's operational style, to establish streamlined processes for areas including financial management, risk management, contractual obligations, and performance monitoring.
Agile Development: Serve as the Business Owner for technologies associated with contracts. Collaborate with product management and system architects on engineering solutions. Engage actively in key Agile ceremonies, including PI planning.
Growth and Strategy: Take the lead in capture, developing winning proposals and creating compelling solutions. Create and implement growth strategies for existing and upcoming contracts. Act as the customer's advocate in product management to help shape company roadmaps based on their requirements.
All other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, business, or a related STEM or business field.
5+ years of relevant professional experience, including 3+ years of program management experience supporting U.S. Government contracts or programs within the aerospace and defense industry.
Experience working in a cleared environment within the past two years.
Demonstrated ability to manage technical development and/or R&D programs, including coordination of multidisciplinary engineering teams.
Strong understanding of product and technology development lifecycles.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with technical teams, customers, and senior leadership.

Desired Qualifications

Master's degree in engineering or a related STEM field.
8+ years of program management experience supporting U.S. Government contracts or programs within the aerospace and defense industry.
Active TS/SCI security clearance, with a read-in within the past two years.

Description

Are you passionate about using intelligence analysis to solve complex challenges in the space domain?

Do you enjoy turning intelligence from multiple sources into actionable data that can inform modeling, simulation, and analysis?

Are you interested in working alongside engineers, modelers, and analysts to help assess and forecast national security space threats?

If so, we're looking for someone like you to join our team at APL!

We are seeking a Space All-Source Intelligence Analyst to support programs within APL's National Security Space Mission Area (NSSMA). You will apply your knowledge of the Intelligence Community (IC) and experience with all-source intelligence analysis to help address critical challenges facing the Department of Defense (DoD) and Intelligence Community in the space domain.

In this role, you will serve as a critical link between intelligence and the technical teams developing high-fidelity modeling, simulation, and analysis (MS&A) capabilities. Rather than focusing primarily on traditional intelligence reporting, you will acquire, analyze, and translate intelligence from multiple classified sources into the quantitative data, parameters, and operational context needed to develop realistic models and simulations. You will collaborate closely with systems engineers, modelers, data scientists, and program teams to ensure our analyses accurately represent real-world threats and operating environments.

As a Space All-Source Intelligence Analyst, you will...

Acquire, analyze, and synthesize intelligence from multiple sources and classified disciplines to develop a comprehensive understanding of space threats and operational environments.
Translate qualitative intelligence assessments into quantitative data, variables, and parameters that can be incorporated into modeling, simulation, and analysis tools.
Collaborate with systems engineers and modelers to integrate intelligence into high-fidelity models used to assess and forecast national security space threats.
Apply intelligence insights to develop realistic operational and training scenarios for complex simulations.
Support model verification and validation by comparing simulation results with available real-world intelligence and identifying discrepancies that may affect model accuracy or fidelity.
Develop and maintain detailed threat and operational environment profiles to ensure models and simulations reflect the most current intelligence available.
Work closely with MS&A engineers, data scientists, analysts, and program managers to define intelligence requirements and effectively integrate intelligence throughout the modeling and analysis lifecycle.
Communicate intelligence findings and technical insights to multidisciplinary teams to support analyses, assessments, and sponsor needs.

Qualifications

You meet our minimum qualifications for the job if you...

B.S. in Intelligence Studies, Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, Data Science or equivalent experience.
At least 5 years of experience in DoD and IC-developed space systems, especially those systems focused on space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), and space situational awareness (SSA)
Expert with IC and DoD processes and protocols for intelligence sharing and collaboration
Demonstrated experience conducting all-source analysis, data and intelligence synthesis, and intelligence analysis and production
Strong written and verbal communication skills with experience preparing executive-level reports, briefings, and intelligence-product publications
Hold an active TS/SCI security clearance. If selected, you will be subject to a government security clearance investigation and must meet the requirements for access to classified information. Eligibility requirements include U.S. citizenship.

You'll go above and beyond our minimum requirements if you...

Advanced degree in Intelligence Studies, National Security, National Strategy, Space Systems Engineering, or related STEM with 8+ years of relevant experience
Assignments to various IC organizations, with at least 3+ years at any one
Demonstrated experience working Space Weapons and Tactics
Experience in Red Team methodologies and threat analysis approaches
Participation in Space Warfare games (i.e., THORS HAMMER, Schriever Wargames, Space Flag)
Current TS//SCI clearance with polygraph, and with existing or previous access to SAP/CAP programs.

Build & manage the plan: Break down complex, ambiguous requirements into a clear project plan with phases, milestones, dependencies, and owners, keeping it current and making trade-offs visible when reality shifts.
Lead requirements gathering: Own the business requirement sessions end to end, facilitating discovery workshops that surface what the client actually needs, documenting requirements in a structured, unambiguous format, managing sign-off, and keeping them traceable through design, build, and testing.
Run the cross-functional team: Coordinate solution architects, engineers, QA, and client stakeholders toward a shared outcome, removing blockers, resolving conflicts, and making sure everyone knows what they own and by when.
Own the client relationship: Be the client's primary point of contact, leading status meetings, steering committee updates, and escalations, setting expectations early, and protecting the relationship even during hard conversations.
Manage scope, risk & change: Hold the line on scope creep, documenting and quantifying changes before work starts, and manage risks and issues proactively with a live view of mitigation plans and early escalation.
Stay technical, report & improve: Understand the architecture, integrations, and configuration decisions well enough to challenge estimates and speak credibly with engineers and technical buyers, produce honest, easy-to-read status reports and executive updates, and feed lessons learned back into delivery methodology.

What Success Looks Like

On-target delivery: Projects land on time, on budget, and within scope, with a clear plan stakeholders trust.
Trusted clients: Clients feel informed and in control throughout the engagement, and would take your call for the next one.
Managed risk: Risks surface early and get managed, so escalations are rare and never a surprise.
Aligned team & clean handoffs: The delivery team is aligned, unblocked, and clear on priorities, and handoffs to support and account teams are clean, with nothing left undocumented.

What You'll Need

Experience: 5+ years managing technical or software implementation projects, ideally in enterprise SaaS, professional services, or a client-facing delivery environment, with a track record of delivering complex, multi-stakeholder projects on time and within budget as the primary delivery owner for enterprise clients.
Technical fluency: You can read a solution design, understand integrations and data flows, and hold your own in a technical discussion without being the engineer.
Requirements & delivery craft: Proven ability to run requirements and discovery sessions and translate them into clear, documented business requirements, plus solid command of project management fundamentals (planning, estimation, dependency management, risk and issue tracking, and change control).
Stakeholder management: Excellent communication, comfort presenting to senior and executive audiences, and the ability to manage scope, timelines, and difficult conversations without losing the relationship.
Ways of working: Organized and calm under pressure, you over-communicate rather than under-communicate, you're direct when a project needs a hard truth and diplomatic when a relationship needs care, and you own outcomes rather than pointing to a process.
Preferred: An earlier technical role (engineering, solution architecture, or implementation consulting); experience delivering configurable enterprise platforms or workflow/automation software; fluency in both agile and traditional delivery and the judgment to know when to use which; experience in a regulated or risk-sensitive domain; PMP, PRINCE2, PSM, or equivalent certification; and exposure to AI-assisted or modern delivery tooling.

Compensation And Benefits

Compensation: Top of market salary + bonuses and equity
Time off: 49 days paid time off
Benefits: PTO, full benefits, retirement and wellness plans
Growth: Professional development support, remote workspace setup bonus
Team building: Annual company offsites in exciting locations around the world

Location

Certa is a remote-first company and we hire globally. We believe strongly in each team member working from the location that they choose. Should Certers wish to meet and work in person, they have 3 lively office locations they can travel to:

London
San Francisco
Jaipur

The perfect place for Certers to collaborate, co-work, and have face-to-face meetings.

Why Certa

Category leadership. Certa was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Third-Party Risk Management Tools - recognition that we're defining the category, not following it.
Industry recognition. We've been honored across the analyst and awards landscape, including Top Tech and Customer Value distinctions in The Hackett Group's 2026 Risk Management SolutionMap, the ProcureTech100 (Advanced AI and Risk Management categories), and Best Overall eProcurement Software in the FinTech Breakthrough Awards.
A top place to work. Certa was named one of Forbes' Best Startup Employers in the US. We're a fast-growing company where you'll wear many hats, ship quickly, and shape decisions that matter.
Real scale with strong backing. We've processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries. We're well-funded by leading investors including Fin Capital, Vertex Ventures, and Point72 Ventures, on the back of an oversubscribed Series B, headed towards Series C.

We're excited to meet you!

jobs.title: Senior Strategic Program Manager
jobs.description:
About XCures

The best of medicine should belong to everyone. Nobody dreams of becoming good at being a patient. We have people to love, things we want to do, and plans we hope to keep. Illness already asks enough of us.

xCures® exists to give healthcare the capacity to care for everyone. Healthcare has more to give. Too much of its time, money, and talent goes into unnecessary work that keeps people waiting and drives up the cost of care. Freeing those resources can make excellent care possible for far more people.

xCures understands a patient’s history across the places they receive care and keeps that understanding current. It puts trusted information in the hands of the people who need it, when they need it, and uses that knowledge to take on more of the administrative work around care. Every extracted data point traces back to the exact document and page it came from.

Our ambition is to empower doctors to make better decisions, enable researchers to develop better treatments faster, and help healthcare organizations serve more people with fewer errors and lower costs. We work with diagnostic labs, providers, telehealth companies, health systems, payers, and consumer health platforms. We are a fully remote, venture-backed team that holds itself to the same standard as our product: trustworthy, precise, and purposeful.

We are building for the lives people want to live.

Here’s Where You’ll Make An Impact

Our most important customers, channel partners, and vendors shape what xCures builds and how quickly we grow. As Senior Strategic Program Manager, you’ll own those relationships end to end. You’ll be their primary point of contact, their advocate inside xCures, and the person who makes sure every commitment is met.

You’ll report to the PMO Director in the Chief Product Officer’s organization and work closely with Product, Engineering, and Data Science. Together, you’ll turn partner needs into clear requirements and roadmap priorities.

This is a new function, and you’ll build it from the ground up: the cadences, the operating model, and the playbooks. You’ll have real autonomy to shape how it works. You may also lead other internal strategic work, such as zero-to-one projects that don’t yet have a natural home. Your impact will show up in partner retention and growth, on-time delivery, a sharper roadmap, and a growing xCures network.

Key Responsibilities

Lead onboarding and implementation for strategic partners, working with Sales on vetting and with technical teams on setup, so each partner goes live on schedule
Build and maintain a single source of truth for every active request, deliverable, and collaboration item across your portfolio, and drive each one to resolution
Build strong, trusted relationships with key customers, channel partners, and vendors, serving as their primary point of contact at xCures
Run partner cadences, including QBRs and recurring status meetings, that keep both sides aligned on priorities, progress, and next steps
Translate partner requests into clear product and engineering requirements, and make sure technical deliverables are well defined and met
Represent partner development interests in roadmap planning, and set clear expectations with partners about what’s coming and when
Own escalations from first report to resolution, bringing in the right people across xCures quickly
Monitor account health and work with Commercial teams to identify and act on growth opportunities
In your first 90 days, take ownership of key partner accounts, establish partner cadences, and stand up a centralized request tracker
Over time, build a mature partner management function, including a repeatable onboarding and implementation playbook
Measure success by partners who feel well served, commitments met as promised, and relationships that grow year over year
Make sure partners are ready when features they requested ship, with the timing, documentation, and support they need to adopt them

Qualifications

Required:

7+ years of professional experience in program management, strategic account management, or client services
Hands-on technical fluency in healthcare interoperability, including interop standards such as C-CDA and FHIR
Strong program and project management skills, with a track record of organizing complex, cross-functional work and seeing it through to completion
A client services background, including experience as the primary point of contact for key accounts
Ability to build trust and influence leaders across departments without direct authority
Ability to translate technical solutions into clear business value for partners and internal teams
A track record of turning manual, repeated work into documented, scalable processes

Bonus Points

Experience with national or regional health data exchange networks and frameworks, such as Carequality, TEFCA, CommonWell, or state and regional HIEs
Strong understanding and demonstrated use of AI tools
Experience working on ML or AI technology solutions

Location

xCures operates in a distributed, remote-first environment, with occasional travel to company offsites or key meetings throughout the year.This role also requires travel to attend industry conferences approximately 2-3 times per year. Candidates may be located anywhere in the United States.

The successful candidate must already have authorization to work in the United States. At this time, xCures does not offer sponsorship. All candidate information will be held in confidence and in accordance with EEOC guidelines. This role also requires travel to attend industry conferences approximately 2-3 times per year.

Additional Considerations

We recognize that people bring a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the requirements listed in a job description. Diversity of experience and skills, combined with a shared passion for healthcare, is what drives us to innovate. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification listed. xCures is an equal opportunity employer, committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Be visionary

Teledyne Technologies Incorporated provides enabling technologies for industrial growth markets that require advanced technology and high reliability. These markets include aerospace and defense, factory automation, air and water quality environmental monitoring, electronics design and development, oceanographic research, deepwater oil and gas exploration and production, medical imaging and pharmaceutical research.

We are looking for individuals who thrive on making an impact and want the excitement of being on a team that wins.

Job Description

Project Manager, Semiconductor IC Design & Development

Bring structure, momentum, and visibility to complex semiconductor development programs. In this role, you will lead projects across the full integrated circuit lifecycle, partnering with engineering, manufacturing, foundry, packaging, test, and business teams to move products from project kickoff through production release. You will combine disciplined project leadership with enough semiconductor technical knowledge to understand dependencies, anticipate risks, and drive timely decisions.

What you'll do

Build and manage integrated schedules from design and verification through layout, tape-out, wafer fabrication, assembly, test, characterization, qualification, and production release.
Define project scope, milestones, deliverables, ownership, budgets, resources, and development gates.
Coordinate cross-functional activities across design, verification, layout, product engineering, test, packaging, manufacturing, and supply chain.
Monitor critical-path dependencies and lead recovery plans when schedules or deliverables are at risk.
Maintain project risk registers and drive mitigation plans for technical, cost, schedule, resource, supply-chain, foundry, packaging, and qualification risks.
Coordinate design reviews, tape-out readiness, technical action items, and verification closure.
Track wafer starts, fabrication cycles, prototype builds, engineering samples, test hardware, and related material dependencies.
Coordinate silicon bring-up, characterization, reliability testing, corrective actions, qualification, and screening activities.
Track development costs and work with functional leaders to address resource constraints and priorities.
Provide concise project reporting covering milestones, schedules, risks, resources, decisions, and accountable actions.

What you need

Strong project planning, scheduling, risk management, problem-solving, and cross-functional leadership skills - required
Strong written and verbal communication skills - required
Understanding of the semiconductor development lifecycle from specification through production - required
5+ years of semiconductor or technical project/program management experience - required
Bachelor’s degree in Electronics Engineering or a related technical discipline - required
Experience managing multiple complete integrated circuit development programs and working with external foundries and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test suppliers - preferred
Project Management Professional certification, relevant master’s degree, and/or experience with Microsoft Project or similar systems - preferred
Knowledge of MIL-STD-883, MIL-PRF-38535, or other applicable high-reliability semiconductor requirements - preferred

What we offer

You’ll have the opportunity to lead technically complex semiconductor programs end to end, work across multiple engineering disciplines, and directly influence how new products progress from concept to production.

What happens next

Submit your application for consideration. Details regarding interview stages, timing, and candidate communications will be shared as part of the recruiting process.

U.S. citizenship, fluency in English, a valid U.S. passport, and the ability to travel domestically and internationally approximately 10% are required. An active Department of Defense security clearance may be required.

$103,200.00-$137,600.000

jobs.title: Technical Project Manager
jobs.description:
Certa (certa.ai) is an AI-native third-party risk management platform that unifies the full third-party lifecycle, from onboarding through continuous monitoring and offboarding. Enterprises from the Fortune 500 to fast-growing startups use our no-code platform to manage vendors, suppliers, and partners across risk, compliance, and ESG. Trusted by Honeywell, Uber, MARS, and Boeing, we've processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries.

We're looking for a Technical Project Manager to own the end-to-end delivery of complex enterprise software implementations. This is a client-facing role at the center of every engagement: you'll translate what a customer needs into a plan, drive a cross-functional team to build it, and keep both sides aligned from kickoff to go-live and beyond. You won't just track tasks, you'll understand the product deeply, engage in technical conversations with solution architects and engineers, lead the business requirement sessions, and make the decisions that keep delivery on track. The best person for this role thinks like an owner of the account, not a coordinator of it.

What You'll Do

Own delivery end to end: Run enterprise implementation projects from kickoff through go-live and stabilization, accountable for scope, timeline, budget, quality, and client satisfaction on every engagement you lead.
Build & manage the plan: Break down complex, ambiguous requirements into a clear project plan with phases, milestones, dependencies, and owners, keeping it current and making trade-offs visible when reality shifts.
Lead requirements gathering: Own the business requirement sessions end to end, facilitating discovery workshops that surface what the client actually needs, documenting requirements in a structured, unambiguous format, managing sign-off, and keeping them traceable through design, build, and testing.
Run the cross-functional team: Coordinate solution architects, engineers, QA, and client stakeholders toward a shared outcome, removing blockers, resolving conflicts, and making sure everyone knows what they own and by when.
Own the client relationship: Be the client's primary point of contact, leading status meetings, steering committee updates, and escalations, setting expectations early, and protecting the relationship even during hard conversations.
Manage scope, risk & change: Hold the line on scope creep, documenting and quantifying changes before work starts, and manage risks and issues proactively with a live view of mitigation plans and early escalation.
Stay technical, report & improve: Understand the architecture, integrations, and configuration decisions well enough to challenge estimates and speak credibly with engineers and technical buyers, produce honest, easy-to-read status reports and executive updates, and feed lessons learned back into delivery methodology.

What Success Looks Like

On-target delivery: Projects land on time, on budget, and within scope, with a clear plan stakeholders trust.
Trusted clients: Clients feel informed and in control throughout the engagement, and would take your call for the next one.
Managed risk: Risks surface early and get managed, so escalations are rare and never a surprise.
Aligned team & clean handoffs: The delivery team is aligned, unblocked, and clear on priorities, and handoffs to support and account teams are clean, with nothing left undocumented.

What You'll Need

Experience: 5+ years managing technical or software implementation projects, ideally in enterprise SaaS, professional services, or a client-facing delivery environment, with a track record of delivering complex, multi-stakeholder projects on time and within budget as the primary delivery owner for enterprise clients.
Technical fluency: You can read a solution design, understand integrations and data flows, and hold your own in a technical discussion without being the engineer.
Requirements & delivery craft: Proven ability to run requirements and discovery sessions and translate them into clear, documented business requirements, plus solid command of project management fundamentals (planning, estimation, dependency management, risk and issue tracking, and change control).
Stakeholder management: Excellent communication, comfort presenting to senior and executive audiences, and the ability to manage scope, timelines, and difficult conversations without losing the relationship.
Ways of working: Organized and calm under pressure, you over-communicate rather than under-communicate, you're direct when a project needs a hard truth and diplomatic when a relationship needs care, and you own outcomes rather than pointing to a process.
Preferred: An earlier technical role (engineering, solution architecture, or implementation consulting); experience delivering configurable enterprise platforms or workflow/automation software; fluency in both agile and traditional delivery and the judgment to know when to use which; experience in a regulated or risk-sensitive domain; PMP, PRINCE2, PSM, or equivalent certification; and exposure to AI-assisted or modern delivery tooling.

Compensation And Benefits

Compensation: Top of market salary + bonuses and equity
Time off: 49 days paid time off
Benefits: PTO, full benefits, retirement and wellness plans
Growth: Professional development support, remote workspace setup bonus
Team building: Annual company offsites in exciting locations around the world

Location

Certa is a remote-first company and we hire globally. We believe strongly in each team member working from the location that they choose. Should Certers wish to meet and work in person, they have 3 lively office locations they can travel to:

London
San Francisco
Jaipur

The perfect place for Certers to collaborate, co-work, and have face-to-face meetings.

Why Certa

Category leadership. Certa was named a Leader in the inaugural 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Third-Party Risk Management Tools - recognition that we're defining the category, not following it.
Industry recognition. We've been honored across the analyst and awards landscape, including Top Tech and Customer Value distinctions in The Hackett Group's 2026 Risk Management SolutionMap, the ProcureTech100 (Advanced AI and Risk Management categories), and Best Overall eProcurement Software in the FinTech Breakthrough Awards.
A top place to work. Certa was named one of Forbes' Best Startup Employers in the US. We're a fast-growing company where you'll wear many hats, ship quickly, and shape decisions that matter.
Real scale with strong backing. We've processed over 10 million entities for 100,000+ users across 120+ countries. We're well-funded by leading investors including Fin Capital, Vertex Ventures, and Point72 Ventures, on the back of an oversubscribed Series B, headed towards Series C.

We're excited to meet you!

A subsidiary of Veolia group, Veolia North America (VNA) is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country’s largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Headquartered in Boston, Mass., Veolia North America has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across the continent.

www.veolianorthamerica.com

Job Description

Veolia is seeking a Data Center Electrical Commissioning - Project Manager to join our Mission Critical department. The selected candidate will represent the company in managing multimillion-dollar, time-sensitive projects for Mission Critical clients. This role involves leading teams of employees, subcontractors, and client vendors to execute critical systems infrastructure projects, including Data Centers, Financial Institutions, and Power Plants.

Responsibilities:

Serve as a Commissioning Project Manager within a team of qualified professionals and degreed engineers.
Manage subcontractors and client vendors on a project-by-project basis.
Assign project tasks and schedules.
Act as a technical subject matter expert for complex mission-critical projects.
Develop procedures, methods, and testing scripts for power, hydraulic, and cooling systems for Data Centers, Financial Institutions, and Power Plants.

Prepare proposals for client RFPs and project pricing requests.
Assist with departmental budgets, KPIs, and financial planning for the Canadian region.
Review and ensure the accuracy of documentation from contractors, subcontractors, and vendors.

Minimum 10 years of experience in the Electrical/Mechanical industry; a Bachelor’s degree is preferred, but an Associate degree from relevant technical programs will be considered.
Equivalent combinations of education and experience are acceptable.
5–10 years of experience in commissioning complex installations and solving construction/operational problems.
Proven experience managing design, energy services, and commissioning projects within scope, budget, and schedule.
Familiarity with NETA, ASHRAE, LEED, and other building codes and industry standards.
Comprehensive understanding of Mission Critical systems related to MEP equipment in Data Centers and Power Plants.
Expertise in electrical systems, including high/medium voltage switchgear, main switchboards, backup generation, UPS systems, and power transfer equipment.
Proficiency in mechanical/thermal systems, such as HVAC equipment, chiller plants, evaporative cooling, and pumping systems.
Knowledge of plant control systems (BMS, SCADA, PLCs) and communication protocols (TCP/IP, Modbus, Canbus).
Familiarity with instrumentation for PID control loops.
Self-motivated with experience in MEP systems design, commissioning, retro-commissioning, and energy modeling for complex buildings.
Ability to perform construction observations, develop functional test plans, and execute tests for electrical and control systems.
Strong people and negotiation skills, time management, and problem-solving abilities.
Capable of explaining technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
Fiscal awareness and ability to mentor direct reports.
P.Eng licensed in the U.S. or Canada (EIT or equivalent professional engineering membership accepted); preferred but not essential.
C.E.T. or equivalent with extensive commissioning experience.
LEED Associate and PMP certification preferred but not mandatory.
Canadian CSA Z462 Electrical Safety qualification or U.S. NFPA 70E equivalent.
Infrared Thermography certification preferred.
Proficiency in computer skills.

Work Environment:

Extensive local, national, and occasional international travel required (40–70% annually).
Typical travel days are Mondays and Fridays, with on-site work on Tuesdays, Wednesdays,
and Thursdays. Veolia provides employees the opportunity to return home on Fridays to
spend weekend with their families, unless specific work requirements necessitate
otherwise.

Occasional work outside normal business hours to accommodate maintenance windows
or weekend schedules.

Work environments include high-energy areas such as central plants, switchgear rooms,
and power transmission areas in Mission Critical facilities.

The ideal candidate will work remotely from Toronto, Canada, with required travel. Veolia is an inclusive company committed to diversity and equal opportunity for all applicants.

Acting today to create the world of tomorrow;

jobs.title: Program Manager, Regulatory Reporting
jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The Software Quality Operations (SWQOps) team is at the heart of ensuring the safety, reliability, and quality of the Waymo Driver. Our mission is to build an adaptable and scalable operation, increasingly powered by AI, to deliver the crucial insights necessary to confidently deploy and grow Waymo's autonomous vehicle service.

Why This Team Is Essential To Waymo's Success

Waymo is undergoing unprecedented growth, rapidly expanding into new cities (targeting ~20 new cities by EOY 2026) and launching new vehicle platforms. SWQ Ops plays a critical role in this expansion, making it possible to scale safely and efficiently. The Regulatory Reporting Operations team within SWQ Ops owns the scaled delivery of datasets and methodologies used to evaluate events of regulatory interest and ensure reporting accuracy as Waymo continues to scale. We are on the front lines of:

De-risking New Deployments: Through meticulous triage of driving and simulated events, issue discovery, and continuous field monitoring, SWQ Ops provides early warnings and critical insights. This "early intervention in RO issue detection" ensures operational resilience and safety, particularly in new and complex environments, which is critical as Waymo enters multiple new cities and ramps up platforms like Ojai.
Enabling International RO & Market Expansion: Our team is deeply integrated into every stage of Waymo's market entry framework, from initial city evaluation (OK2Plan) to scaling operations (OK2Scale). We provide the necessary data analysis, policy development, and quality assurance to unblock critical milestones, preventing slowdowns in market expansion velocity.
Data Flywheel: Supporting the development of a single, automated, end-to-end machine learning flywheel for the entire Waymo Driver. A successful flywheel will be the core engine for scaling our technology, enabling faster international expansion, quicker remediation of driving issues, and a significant reduction in the engineering effort required to maintain and improve the driver.
Driving Engineering Velocity: By handling the vital work of performance evaluation, issue deep-dives, and data set curation, SWQOps collaborates heavily and allows Waymo's Engineering, SysEng, Simulation, and Data Science teams to focus on their core tasks of developing and improving the Waymo Driver.
Workflow Incubation & Development: Incubating high-impact workflows and ensuring readiness for automation and long-term operational excellence.

You Will

Drive outcomes for large and complex technical operations programs that span multiple organizations. Develop and drive execution on strategic roadmaps, own forecasting and resource planning.
Partner with the Regulatory Compliance team to operationalize reporting requirements and be responsible for standing up new workflows and scaling existing workflows to support US and International expansions.
Define program / workflow KPIs and SLAs. Drive high-quality outcomes through deployments with a global vendor workforce.
Drive workflow transformation efforts to meet evolving business needs. Partner with Engineering to design, test, and deploy cutting-edge Machine Learning (ML) and Generative AI (Gen-AI) models and tools to drive step-change improvements in issue discovery & detection, triage efficiency, and quality assurance.
Communicate overall program status, risks and current priorities to executive stakeholders. Drive strategic decisions making across functions.
Mentor a high-performing team of Technical Specialists, fostering a culture of "quality-first" in a high-velocity environment.

You Have

Bachelor's degree in technical, legal or business discipline
10+ years of experience managing complex, tech-enabled operations and experience working across cross-functional partners (Legal, Product, Engineering, Data Science, Systems Engineering) to drive outcomes
5+ years of people management experience
Experience in Regulatory Compliance, Vehicle Qualification, or similar domains, and ability to assess and operationalize legal reporting requirements
Proven ability to manage complex technical operations programs, including structuring project plans, identifying dependencies, and driving execution
Ability to thrive in a high ambiguity, dynamic environment

We Prefer

Experience working with offshore teams / multiple local operations hubs
Experience within A / V space
Increased competency in supporting all phases of the machine learning development lifecycle, from data preparation and training to validation, deployment, and continuous monitoring
Experience with Lean / Six Sigma process improvement methodologies

Benefits

In accordance with Washington state law, we are highlighting our comprehensive benefits package, which is available to all eligible US based employees. Benefits for this role include:

Health, dental, vision, life, disability insurance

Paid Time Off: 20 days of vacation per year, accruing at a rate of 6.15 hours per pay period for the first five years of employment

jobs.title: Sr Staff Technical Program Manager – Therapy Optimization
jobs.description:
The Company

Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Dexcom began as a small company with a big dream: To forever change how diabetes is managed. To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We are broadening our vision beyond diabetes to empower people to take control of health. That means personalized, actionable insights aimed at solving important health challenges. To continue what we've started: Improving human health.

We are driven by thousands of ambitious, passionate people worldwide who are willing to fight like warriors to earn the trust of our customers by listening, serving with integrity, thinking big, and being dependable. We've already changed millions of lives and we're ready to change millions more. Our future ambition is to become a leading consumer health technology company while continuing to develop solutions for serious health conditions. We'll get there by constantly reinventing unique biosensing-technology experiences. Though we've come a long way from our small company days, our dreams are bigger than ever. The opportunity to improve health on a global scale stands before us.

Meet the team

Our Product Technical Program Management team leads Dexcom’s Clinical Products from concept through commercialization. Therapy Optimization
is one of our most exciting areas: Smart Basal, Dexcom’s first digital therapeutic, is a CGM-based program that delivers long-acting (basal) insulin dose recommendations. Programs like this bring together software, algorithm, cloud platform, clinical, regulatory, quality, human factors, and commercial teams in ways that go beyond traditional device development.

A successful Sr Staff Technical Program Manager
is a cross-functional leader recognized by peers and functional leadership for guiding teams from different functional backgrounds and reporting lines. They own program scope, deliverables, roadmap, and schedule; communicate clearly; foster collaboration; keep teams motivated; and drive data-driven decisions that weigh product, platform, and program trade-offs. They have a proven record of leading technical development programs from feasibility to commercialization in the medical device or digital health space, along with the business and organizational awareness to make trade-off recommendations that optimize outcomes for multiple stakeholders.

Where you come in

You will lead Therapy Optimization programs, such as Smart Basal, along with other Digital Solutions programs, from planning and development through verification and validation, clinical studies, regulatory submissions, and launch.
You will lead cross-functional core teams and build integrated plans across Software, Algorithm, Cloud Platform, Clinical, Regulatory, Quality, Human Factors, Medical Affairs, Product Management, Commercial, and Legal.
You will coordinate synchronized delivery across multiple software releases (app, clinician portal, backend, and algorithm) and align program milestones with broader product and software roadmaps.
You will manage regulatory and clinical timelines, including FDA submissions and EU MDR/notified body pathways, and make sure change-impact evidence and design control documentation are planned and delivered on schedule.
You will identify risks early, drive mitigation plans, and resolve trade-offs among scope, schedule, quality, and compliance, escalating to leadership when decisions are needed.
You will communicate program strategy, scope, deliverables, schedules, status, and recommendations regularly to functional and executive leadership and through governance forums.
You will build a culture of accountability and collaboration by removing barriers, resolving conflict promptly, running retrospectives, and sharing lessons learned across programs.
You will mentor team members and provide candid feedback to them and their managers.

What Makes You Successful

Demonstrated technical program management and leadership of a complex medical device or software-as-a-medical-device (SaMD) program that introduced new technology to market, with strong technical, cross-functional, and risk-management leadership.
Experience across software and digital health disciplines such as mobile apps, cloud platforms, algorithms, and cybersecurity, ideally for therapy, dosing, or decision-support products.
Experience with regulatory filings for novel medical technologies through FDA (e.g., 510(k)) and/or EU MDR pathways, and with clinical study coordination.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and be comfortable with ambiguity, shifting priorities, and trade-offs.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, conveying technical and business information clearly in documents, reports, and presentations at all levels.
Expertise with stage-gate product development and/or agile software development frameworks (medical preferred).
Experience managing stakeholders and external partners at all technical and leadership levels, driving critical decisions and resolving competing interests.
Experience in the medical device industry, with proven ability to work within a Quality System compliant with FDA Design Control regulations (21 CFR 820.30).
Training in Six Sigma, design of experiments, and statistical methods is a plus.

What You’ll Get

A front row seat to life-changing CGM technology. Learn about our brave #dexcomwarriors community.
A full and comprehensive benefits program.
Growth opportunities on a global scale.
Access to career development through in-house learning programs and/or qualified tuition reimbursement.
An exciting and innovative, industry-leading organization committed to our employees, customers, and the communities we serve.

Travel Required

5–15%

Experience And Education Requirements

Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree in a technical discipline, and a minimum of 13+ years related experience or a Master’s degree and 8+ years equivalent industry experience or a PhD and 5+ years of experience.

Flex Workplace:
Your primary location will be a home office. You will not have an assigned workstation and will work with your manager to determine office visit needs. You must live within commuting distance of your assigned Dexcom site (typically 75 miles/120km).

This role is critical to advancing SIU’s Intelligence & Innovation strategy through the design, development, and execution of proactive fraud detection, analytics, and investigative intelligence programs. The position serves as a key driver in identifying emerging fraud risks, transforming complex data into actionable intelligence, and delivering innovative solutions that enhance SIU’s effectiveness, operational efficiency, and enterprise value.

Supports the strategic planning, development, and execution of SIU proactive anti-fraud detection, tools and analytics programs, initiatives, and priorities to strengthen the SIUs Intelligence & Innovation operations.
Transforms large and complex data sets into defensible, actionable analytical insights that support investigative lead generation, case development, fraud prevention initiatives, and data-driven decision-making while ensuring compliance with enterprise governance standards and regulatory requirements.
